observations: The single CoJ process reached normal outer run_end and produced a complete evidence package, but the user rejected the playability gate visually and interactively.

Menus still lacked useful controller semantics: only the already-selected/default option could be activated reliably, the pointer did not drive the hovered item, there was no distinct accept/back mapping, and startup content still could not be skipped reliably.
The visible flat-theater ray did not originate from the Sense controller as expected.

Walking, running and jumping remained visibly jerky; the user reproduced the same poor motion with keyboard input, which makes the high-volume synchronous VR instrumentation path a concrete performance suspect rather than a controller-only mapping problem.

The arms still felt too short. The measured native two-bone chain remained approximately 49.843 game units, but clamp was strongly asymmetric at 27.09 percent left versus 70.82 percent right; this does not support simply scaling both bones.
Shots still originated from the gaze/native player point rather than the weapon/controller.

Physical crouch moved the HMD behind/outside the avatar so the user could see the whole body; expected behavior is to enter the native crouch state and bend the avatar legs while preserving first-person ownership.
